newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cuba's Lage visits Brazil on Latam support tour.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's Lage visits Brazil on Latam support tour.

text.p: Cuban Vice President Carlos Lage met with Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso Friday to ask for support against what Havana fears is a tightening of the U.S. embargo.

"It was an excellent meeting, very friendly and we touched on a lot of subjects," Lage said after a one-hour meeting with the Brazilian leader. "We have been meeting with all the governments of Latin America regarding the U.S. blockade of Cuba and the new measures to implement it."

Cuban president Fidel Castro has sent his most senior officials on a whirlwind tour of the region to ask heads of state for their support against what he fears are moves in the U.S. Congress to further isolate the Communist island.
Lage, Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina and Investment Minister Ibrahim Ferradez have been delivering letters from Castro to leaders across Latin America since last week.

Cuba fears new amendments to a foreign relations bill will tighten the Helms Burton Act, which seeks to punish foreign companies investing in the island. The U.S. State Department has denied the amendments will have much effect.
An aide to Cardoso said Brazil had already stated its opposition to the Helms Burton law. He also said a law currently in Brazil's Congress would free up about 20,000 tonnes of food for Cuba.
